title: fix(memory): keep the most recent messages in Weaviate filter-only search

files.patch:
@@ -313,8 +313,7 @@ def search(
 
         Returns:
             List of matching messages sorted by relevance (if query provided)
-            or potentially unsorted/timestamp-sorted (if only filters provided).
-            Note: Sorting for filter-only results happens in the Memory class if needed.
+            or the most recent matches, oldest first (if only filters provided).
         """
         if self._vector_store is None:
             raise WeaviateMemoryError("Weaviate vector store not initialized.")
@@ -350,8 +349,11 @@ def search(
                     filters=prepared_filters, content_key=self.content_property_name
                 )
                 retrieved_messages = [self._document_to_message(doc) for doc in documents]
+                # filter_documents has no ordering, so truncating it would keep an arbitrary
+                # subset. Keep the most recent messages, oldest first, like get_all and InMemory.search.
+                retrieved_messages.sort(key=lambda msg: msg.metadata.get("timestamp", 0))
                 if effective_limit > 0:
-                    retrieved_messages = retrieved_messages[:effective_limit]
+                    retrieved_messages = retrieved_messages[-effective_limit:]

@@ -148,3 +149,27 @@ def test_postgres_backends_of_one_process_create_their_table_once(mocker):
 
     assert executed.call_count == 4  # the lock, the table and its two indices
     assert "pg_advisory_xact_lock" in executed.call_args_list[0].args[0]
+
+
+def test_weaviate_filter_only_search_with_limit_returns_the_most_recent(mocker):
+    """filter_documents returns an unordered set; the limit must keep the newest, oldest first."""
+    from dynamiq.memory.backends.weaviate import Weaviate
+
+    mocker.patch.object(Weaviate, "model_post_init", lambda self, __context: None)
+    backend = Weaviate.model_construct(collection_name="c", content_property_name="message_content")
+    store = mocker.Mock()
+    # Stored out of order, as a vector DB is free to return them.
+    order = [5, 1, 9, 0, 7, 3, 8, 2, 6, 4]
+    store.filter_documents.return_value = [
+        Document(
+            id=str(i),
+            content=f"msg-{i}",
+            metadata={"message_role": "user", "message_timestamp": float(i), "message_id": str(i)},
+        )
+        for i in order
+    ]
+    backend._vector_store = store
+
+    result = backend.search(query=None, filters={"field": "user_id", "operator": "==", "value": "u"}, limit=LIMIT)
+
+    assert [m.content for m in result] == ["msg-7", "msg-8", "msg-9"]
